assumptions: Existing legacy tools and commands remain compatibility surfaces until replacement wrapper parity is validated.
Some current schemas still use legacy audit/check/proof field names; migration tasks preserve compatibility while moving user-facing vocabulary.
Roadmap duplicate-prevention can over-refine related planning tasks; planning repaired TASK-077 and recorded evidence.
non_goals: Do not implement source changes in planning loop.
Do not create an umbrella/container task that only closes other tasks.
Do not remove compatibility tools/commands before replacement coverage exists.
Do not publish, release, push, or perform destructive actions.
risks: High migration risk across public commands/tools and validation policy; tasks require source-contract, gateway, and targeted smoke coverage.
Existing planned/active older sprints overlap conceptual domains; implementation sessions must claim narrow scopes and avoid unrelated sprint work.
Terminology migration may conflict with existing tool/schema names; compatibility metadata must be explicit.
